items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: The transcript contains no mention of George Louis by the interviewee, nor any interaction or relationship described between the interviewee (Kid Howard) and George Louis. The name 'George Louis' appears only in the interviewer's comparison.

ctx.x: I would say so. I mean Louis Armstrong is, I mean Louis Armstrong takes in a lot of people that are not particularly interested in jazz but because of the outstanding amount of publicity he gets and because he also plays humorous versions of numbers that are well known to a lot of old timers because you might realize that in Europe it's the young people that go for jazz, college students and all the young boys and girls. And Louis Armstrong was just the first band to come over and make a success out of jazz in…
He draws better than George Louis.

He draws better than anybody. I mean he draws better than most classical singers or anything. I think he made ten concerts in the KB Hall last time he was there and that holds about four thousand people and that means that forty thousand people out of Copenhagen came to see him, you know. And that was just a year after he was there last time and it goes like that every time between forty and sixty thousand people and that's outstanding. I don't think there's a single entertainer in the whole world that can do…
